Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Planner hints:

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 satisfies the preferred WARRANTY position on every material term:

- **Services standard (19.1):** professional and workmanlike, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus material conformity to documentation and specifications.
- **Duration (19.2):** 90 days for Deliverables measured from delivery *or acceptance, whichever is later*; hosted Services warranted for the entire subscription term — better than the preferred 12-month software period.
- **Additional warranties (19.3):** no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution, no contaminating open source.
- **Remedy (19.4):** prompt re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid; expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Disclaimer (19.5):** limited to implied warranties and expressly carves out express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so it does not swallow the express warranty.

This also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

content.text: No liquidated-damages, penalty, or early-termination-fee provision payable by us appears anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee amount payable by Customer: searches for "liquidated damages", "termination fee", "penalty" and "shall pay" return nothing of that kind, and the termination provisions (§§ 9.1–9.3, 9.5, 10.1–10.2, 27.3) impose no exit charge on us — § 27.3 expressly allows termination "without penalty" with a refund. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). Two adjacent economics were considered and are not LD under this rule: § 2.1's USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment is a minimum-commitment term addressed under MINCOMMIT (not double-flagged here), and § 22.2's audit cost-shifting is a conditional reimbursement of actual costs plus the undisputed shortfall, not a stipulated damages amount. Nothing to redline.

input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is squarely the playbook's walk-away position: a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit, and it fails the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and sits uneasily with Section 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges. Redline replaces the commitment with the preferred position (payment for Services ordered or used only); the fallback 12-month reducible commitment with a true-up is offered in the comment if a commitment is commercially required.

proposal.summary: Replace three-year take-or-pay minimum with no minimum commitment; fees payable for ordered/used Services only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with our standard position that fees are payable only for Services ordered or used. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss limiting it to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty. This also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment.

That is squarely the playbook's walk-away position: a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit, and it fails the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and sits uneasily with Section 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges. Redline replaces the commitment with the preferred position (payment for Services ordered or used only); the fallback 12-month reducible commitment with a true-up is offered in the comment if a commitment is commercially required.

proposal.summary: Replace three-year take-or-pay minimum with no minimum commitment; fees payable for ordered/used Services only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced Section 2.1 with our standard position that fees are payable only for Services ordered or used. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss limiting it to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty. This also removes the conflict with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Customer is obligated to pay only for Services ordered under an Order Form or actually used, and no shortfall, unused-capacity, or similar charge applies.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

- **What I checked:** full-text searches for "liquidated damages", "termination fee", "penalty", "remaining contract value", "shall pay"; the termination and post-termination sections (§§ 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2), fees/disputes (§§ 7.1–7.5), liability (§§ 21.1–21.4), audit (§§ 22.1–22.3), and force majeure (§ 27.3).
- **Result:** No liquidated damages, stipulated penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee charge is payable by Juniper Ridge. § 27.3 in fact lets us terminate "without penalty" with a prepaid-fee refund, and § 10.2 runs refunds in our favour. This sits at the **preferred** position, so no redline was proposed.
- **Noted, not flagged:** § 2.1's USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment is the closest economic exposure but is a minimum-commitment term reviewed under MINCOMMIT — not double-flagged here. § 22.2's audit cost-shifting is reimbursement of actual costs plus the undisputed shortfall (and only above a 5% underpayment threshold), not a stipulated damages amount.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion obligation as new Section 10.3
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit clause because Section 10 refers to a transition period but contains no obligation to help us transition or to return our Customer Data (Section 11, cross-referenced in 16.5, does not exist). Our playbook requires up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance if six months is an issue.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for export all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: deviation (walk-away term) at § 2.1 (p0012).**

- **Issue:** § 2.1 binds us to a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook's walk-away scenario, failing even the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty).
- **Internal conflict:** § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that Customer has made *no* minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** § 2.1 replaced with no minimum/volume/take-or-pay commitment; payment only for Services ordered or actually used, with no shortfall or unused-capacity charge. The fallback (12-month reducible commitment with true-up) is offered in the comment if a commitment is commercially necessary.

input.quote: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no post-termination transition assistance or data return/export obligation. Section 10 only ends access after "any agreed transition period" (with no obligation to agree or provide one) and addresses Deliverables and refunds; Section 15 covers processing but not return or deletion; Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" and Section 11 does not exist in the document. Searches for transition, export, and deletion terms return nothing else. The rule therefore fails both the preferred and fallback positions (no assistance period, no export window, no certified deletion), so we insert a new Section 10.3 at the preferred position, with the 90-day fallback offered in the comment.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Searches for transition, export, and deletion terms return nothing else. The rule therefore fails both the preferred and fallback positions (no assistance period, no export window, no certified deletion), so we insert a new Section 10.3 at the preferred position, with the 90-day fallback offered in the comment.

**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation exists in the Agreement.

What I verified:
- **Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination)** only ends access "after any agreed transition period" (§10.1) and covers Deliverable delivery and refunds (§10.2) — no obligation on Vendor to provide assistance or return data.
- **Section 15 (Customer Data and Privacy)** governs processing limits only; no return, export, or deletion mechanic.
- **Section 16.5** defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15" — but **Section 11 does not exist** in the document, so the cross-reference is a dead end.
- Text searches for "transition", "export", "delet", and "machine-readable" surfaced nothing else usable.

This fails both the preferred and the fallback position (no assistance period, no export window, no certified deletion), so I inserted a new §10.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, Customer Data returned in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (with routine backup/legal retention carve-out to keep it acceptable to Vendor). The 90-day fallback is flagged in the negotiation comment.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement form

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The agreement is well drafted in several places that matter to us — the liability cap, assignment and change of control, renewal mechanics, the performance warranty, audit rights and Vendor insurance all sit at our preferred position and need no redlines.

The problems are concentrated in two areas. First, **the agreement has no indemnification clause at all**: Section 20 is absent from the document even though Sections 9.3 and 19.4 depend on it, and Section 9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," leaving a broken reference. That is walk-away territory and must be fixed by inserting Section 20.

Second, the agreement loads a cluster of one-sided restrictions onto us that our playbook treats as walk-away items and that **contradict Section 12.3**, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. These are the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in Section 2.1, the disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2 (which is both a de facto exclusivity/ROFR and an MFN running against us), the 24-month unlimited-scope Customer non-compete and the 24-month full no-hire in the two Sections 12.4. Deleting or narrowing them restores internal consistency as well as our playbook position.

Three further gaps round out the list: Vendor owns every Deliverable we pay for under Section 14.2 with only a revocable, term-limited licence back; there is no Customer termination for convenience across a three-year committed term; there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation; and Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, in direct conflict with Section 28.2's submission to the New York County courts.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 20 absent (cross-referenced at §§ 9.3, 19.4; see § 19.5) | No indemnity anywhere; broken cross-reference to § 20.5. Insert Section 20. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; only a revocable, term-limited licence to us. Flip ownership with assignment; § 14.3 Vendor Technology unaffected. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full Excluded Claims set (§ 21.3). No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Customer may assign to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted; no repricing on our change of control (§ 24.4). No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match before engaging another provider is a de facto exclusivity/ROFR, unlimited in scope and term. Delete. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages or exit fee; § 27.3 permits termination without penalty with refund. No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and omits Affiliates/contractors, unlike §§ 13.1–13.3. Conform to Section 13. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (non-compete) | 24-month post-term, undefined scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions barred. Delete and rely on § 12.3. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 9.3 (see § 2.1, § 8.1) | No Customer convenience right across a three-year take-or-pay term. Add 30-day right with pro-rata refund as new § 9.4; conform § 2.1. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | One audit per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access; cost-shifting only above 5% underpayment. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; conflicts with § 28.2 (New York County). Substitute New York law and forum. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights. Replace with pay-for-what-is-ordered. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (no-hire) | One-sided 24-month full no-hire covering all Vendor employees, overriding general-advertising carve-outs. Narrow to mutual 12-month non-solicit. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3% (§ 8.3). No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (see § 16.5) | No transition assistance, export window or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. Insert new § 10.3. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties, hosted Services warranted for the full subscription term, non-exclusive remedies; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M through term plus one year. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following are walk-away positions under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing Section 20).** With no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, we carry infringement and regulatory exposure ourselves. We propose the preferred package: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications); standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law; and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in § 20.5 to repair the § 9.3 cross-reference.
2. **Section 2.1 take-or-pay.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment "without reduction or termination rights" is squarely walk-away. Fallback if a commitment is commercially required: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
3. **Section 7.2 disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusivity/ROFR and Customer-side MFN; unlimited as to product, term and comparability. Deletion is the smallest fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.
4. **Section 12.4 Customer non-compete.** 24 months post-term, undefined competing scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions expressly barred. Delete; we can discuss a narrowed restriction tied to a specific named product if Vendor identifies one.
5. **Section 12.4 no-hire.** A one-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees regardless of how they apply. We have narrowed it to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, personnel directly involved in the Services, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no-hire deleted); our preferred position remains no restriction on us.
6. **Section 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and an exclusive foreign forum. We align 28.1 with 28.2 (New York law, New York County courts), leaving §§ 28.2–28.3 intact.
7. **Section 14.2 Deliverable licence.** A revocable, term-limited grant to work product we commissioned and paid for approaches walk-away under the licence-scope rule; it is addressed together with the ownership flip.

---

## Next steps

1. **Confirm commercial mandate on Section 2.1.** Whether we can accept any minimum commitment, and if so whether the 12-month reducible fallback with a true-up is acceptable, drives the § 2.1 and § 9.4 redlines together.
2. **Send the redline as a package.** Insert Section 20 (indemnification, including § 20.5 remedies); insert new § 10.3 (transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion, with a 90-day fallback offered in comment); insert new § 9.4 (30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund) and conform § 2.1; flip § 14.2 Deliverable ownership with assignment and conform the Deliverable licence to Section 13; delete § 7.2 and the § 12.4 non-compete; narrow the § 12.4 no-hire; and substitute New York law and forum in § 28.1.
3. **Flag the drafting defects separately to Vendor's counsel.** The absent Section 20, the absent Section 11 referenced by § 16.5, the empty Section 23, the duplicated Section 12.4 numbering and the 28.1/28.2 forum conflict are internal inconsistencies rather than positions, and framing them that way should speed acceptance.
4. **Use Section 12.3 as the lever.** Vendor has already acknowledged there that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment; every deletion we seek in items 2–5 above simply gives that acknowledgement effect.

# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement form

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The agreement is well drafted in several places that matter to us — the liability cap, assignment and change of control, renewal mechanics, the performance warranty, audit rights and Vendor insurance all sit at our preferred position and need no redlines.

The problems are concentrated in two areas. First, **the agreement has no indemnification clause at all**: Section 20 is absent from the document even though Sections 9.3 and 19.4 depend on it, and Section 9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," leaving a broken reference. That is walk-away territory and must be fixed by inserting Section 20.

Second, the agreement loads a cluster of one-sided restrictions onto us that our playbook treats as walk-away items and that **contradict Section 12.3**, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. These are the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in Section 2.1, the disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2 (which is both a de facto exclusivity/ROFR and an MFN running against us), the 24-month unlimited-scope Customer non-compete and the 24-month full no-hire in the two Sections 12.4. Deleting or narrowing them restores internal consistency as well as our playbook position.

Three further gaps round out the list: Vendor owns every Deliverable we pay for under Section 14.2 with only a revocable, term-limited licence back; there is no Customer termination for convenience across a three-year committed term; there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation; and Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, in direct conflict with Section 28.2's submission to the New York County courts.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 20 absent (cross-referenced at §§ 9.3, 19.4; see § 19.5) | No indemnity anywhere; broken cross-reference to § 20.5. Insert Section 20. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; only a revocable, term-limited licence to us. Flip ownership with assignment; § 14.3 Vendor Technology unaffected. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with full Excluded Claims set (§ 21.3). No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Customer may assign to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted; no repricing on our change of control (§ 24.4). No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match before engaging another provider is a de facto exclusivity/ROFR, unlimited in scope and term. Delete. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No Customer-payable liquidated damages or exit fee; § 27.3 permits termination without penalty with refund. No redline. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and omits Affiliates/contractors, unlike §§ 13.1–13.3. Conform to Section 13. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (non-compete) | 24-month post-term, undefined scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions barred. Delete and rely on § 12.3. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 9.3 (see § 2.1, § 8.1) | No Customer convenience right across a three-year take-or-pay term. Add 30-day right with pro-rata refund as new § 9.4; conform § 2.1. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | One audit per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access; cost-shifting only above 5% underpayment. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; conflicts with § 28.2 (New York County). Substitute New York law and forum. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor; conflicts with § 12.3. Delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights. Replace with pay-for-what-is-ordered. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (no-hire) | One-sided 24-month full no-hire covering all Vendor employees, overriding general-advertising carve-outs. Narrow to mutual 12-month non-solicit. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3% (§ 8.3). No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (see § 16.5) | No transition assistance, export window or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. Insert new § 10.3. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 | Professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties, hosted Services warranted for the full subscription term, non-exclusive remedies; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M through term plus one year. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following are walk-away positions under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing Section 20).** With no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, we carry infringement and regulatory exposure ourselves. We propose the preferred package: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; customary exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications); standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law; and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in § 20.5 to repair the § 9.3 cross-reference.
2. **Section 2.1 take-or-pay.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment "without reduction or termination rights" is squarely walk-away. Fallback if a commitment is commercially required: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
3. **Section 7.2 disclose-and-match.** Walk-away as both exclusivity/ROFR and Customer-side MFN; unlimited as to product, term and comparability. Deletion is the smallest fix and restores consistency with § 12.3.
4. **Section 12.4 Customer non-compete.** 24 months post-term, undefined competing scope, unlimited territory, acquisitions expressly barred. Delete; we can discuss a narrowed restriction tied to a specific named product if Vendor identifies one.
5. **Section 12.4 no-hire.** A one-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees regardless of how they apply. We have narrowed it to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from the end of the individual's involvement, personnel directly involved in the Services, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no-hire deleted); our preferred position remains no restriction on us.
6. **Section 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and an exclusive foreign forum. We align 28.1 with 28.2 (New York law, New York County courts), leaving §§ 28.2–28.3 intact.
7. **Section 14.2 Deliverable licence.** A revocable, term-limited grant to work product we commissioned and paid for approaches walk-away under the licence-scope rule; it is addressed together with the ownership flip.

---

## Next steps

1. **Confirm commercial mandate on Section 2.1.** Whether we can accept any minimum commitment, and if so whether the 12-month reducible fallback with a true-up is acceptable, drives the § 2.1 and § 9.4 redlines together.
2. **Send the redline as a package.** Insert Section 20 (indemnification, including § 20.5 remedies); insert new § 10.3 (transition assistance and Customer Data return/deletion, with a 90-day fallback offered in comment); insert new § 9.4 (30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund) and conform § 2.1; flip § 14.2 Deliverable ownership with assignment and conform the Deliverable licence to Section 13; delete § 7.2 and the § 12.4 non-compete; narrow the § 12.4 no-hire; and substitute New York law and forum in § 28.1.
3. **Flag the drafting defects separately to Vendor's counsel.** The absent Section 20, the absent Section 11 referenced by § 16.5, the empty Section 23, the duplicated Section 12.4 numbering and the 28.1/28.2 forum conflict are internal inconsistencies rather than positions, and framing them that way should speed acceptance.
4. **Use Section 12.3 as the lever.** Vendor has already acknowledged there that we have made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment; every deletion we seek in items 2–5 above simply gives that acknowledgement effect.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant clauses.** Sections 8, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24 sit at or above our preferred position; we should protect them in any exchange of drafts.
